b1-unit-56.56.1 Gap Year Diaries: I'm not a morning:
Danny: Welcome back to Gap Year Diaries. I have a confession: I'm not a morning person. Since the language school gave me the seven a.m. classes, getting up has been a nightmare. So today Ana is here to help me.
Ana: Hi everyone! Doctor Ana is here to save Danny.
Danny: So what time do you get up?
Ana: At five-thirty when I work the morning shift. And I get out of bed right away. No snooze button.
Danny: Five-thirty! How do you do that?
Ana: First, plan the night before. Get your clothes and your bag ready before you go to bed. Then in the morning you can get going in ten minutes.
Danny: I usually spend twenty minutes looking for my keys.
Ana: Exactly. Second, leave your phone out of the bedroom. If you check messages in bed, your brain gets too excited, and you can't get to sleep.
Danny: But my phone is my alarm clock!
Ana: Then get a real alarm clock. Third, let some light in. Leave the curtains a little open, so the sun can wake you up naturally.
Danny: What about coffee? I drink coffee at night when I'm planning my classes.
Ana: Bad idea. Try to avoid coffee in the late afternoon and evening. In the morning, drink a glass of water as soon as you get up, and have breakfast. It helps you get off to a good start.
Danny: Anything else?
Ana: The most important thing is to have something to look forward to. If you're excited about your day, it's much easier to get out of bed.
Danny: Like Mrs. Lima's cheese bread at breakfast.
Ana: If that's what gets you up, perfect!
Danny: OK, listeners. Starting tomorrow, I'm getting up at six. Ana will call me to check.
Ana: I'll call at one minute past six!
